extraction_text: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about the best and most pure bathing places among all pilgrimage sites.

attributes.relationship: Grandson asks grandfather for spiritual wisdom

extraction_text: Bhishma explains that all bathing places have their merits, but he will describe which is purer for the wise.
Bhishma describes Manasa as a bathing place for those guided by eternal truth - deep, clear, pure, with truth as water and firmness as lake.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Sacred site Manasa with symbolic qualities

extraction_text: Bhishma defines a pure bathing place as one where bathing makes people desireless, gentle, truthful, reliable, loving, compassionate, self-controlled, peaceful.

attributes.action: Describes transformative effects of true purity

extraction_text: Bhishma states that people who are free from selfishness, overcome pride, transcend dualities, renounce worldly things, live on alms are themselves bathing places.

attributes.action: Equates purified individuals with sacred sites

extraction_text: Bhishma declares that those who know truth and abandon ego are the supreme bathing places.

attributes.action: Elevates enlightened beings above physical sites

extraction_text: Bhishma explains that true bathing is not wetting limbs with water but cleansing oneself through restraint.
Bhishma teaches that knowledge brings purity, and purity of action leads to purity of mind.
Bhishma states that those who know truth and understand soul bathe in Manasa with inner light and knowledge of Brahman.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Bathing with spiritual qualities rather than water

extraction_text: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira that he has described internal bathing places within humans, and will now describe external ones on earth.
Bhishma explains that just as humans show purity characteristics, many earthly places and waters show divine characteristics.
Bhishma concludes that by invoking bathing places, bathing there, or offering ancestral rites, people can cleanse sins and attain heaven after death.
Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about the highest principle governing the cycle of rebirth and what accompanies a person after death.
Bhishma directs Yudhishthira to ask the learned Brihaspati, who arrives as they speak.

attributes.relationship: Bhishma defers to Brihaspati's superior knowledge

extraction_text: Yudhishthira respectfully greets Brihaspati and repeats his question about what accompanies a person after death.
Brihaspati explains that all beings are born alone, die alone, and face difficulties alone; after death, only Dharma (righteousness) follows the abandoned body.

attributes.key_point: Dharma is the eternal companion after death

extraction_text: Yudhishthira asks about how Dharma follows the body after death.
Brihaspati explains that earth, wind, space, water, light, mind, and soul witness all righteous and unrighteous actions of beings.
Brihaspati states that after death, Dharma follows the life force along with these witnesses.
Yudhishthira asks how semen is produced.
Brihaspati explains that the gods residing in the body (earth, wind, space, water, light, and mind) consume food, and when satisfied, semen is produced in pure-souled people.
Brihaspati describes that after semen production comes union of husband and wife and embryo formation.
Yudhishthira asks how a person is actually born.
Brihaspati explains that once an embryo is formed, it is grasped by the elements, and when later abandoned by them, it goes to another destination, thus creating new life.
Brihaspati adds that the gods residing in the five elements observe all human actions, good and bad.
Yudhishthira asks where life goes to experience suffering or happiness after abandoning skin, bones, and flesh.
Brihaspati explains that life actually carries Dharma quickly into semen, then approaches a menstruating woman, seizing the opportunity to cause conception.
阎摩王的使者决定生命出生后的受苦和死亡等大事，陷入轮回和受苦是不可避免的。
生命从出生起以正法为标准，依照过去所做的业享受果报。
如果生命从降生起就竭尽全力履行正法，来世会生而为人并长享幸福。
如果生命始终履行正法但间有背离，来世会先享福而后受苦。
如果尽做违犯正法的事，会去往阎摩掌管的地方受苦，来世进入畜生的子宫。
生命常会陷于迷惑，由于做业不同而在来世进入不同的子宫。
法论、历史传说及其他圣诗中说，世上寿数有限的生命一概注定要去阎摩掌管的可怕地方。
学习过四吠陀的再生者从堕落的人手里接受施舍，死后堕入驴子的子宫，作为驴子生活十五年。
驴子死后生为公牛生活七年，公牛死后生为梵罗刹生活三个月，然后复生为婆罗门。
婆罗门为堕落的人举行祭祀，来世堕入蠕虫的子宫生活十五年。
从蠕虫脱身后生成驴子五年，然后公猪五年，狗一年，最后复生为人。
丧失理智的学生对老师犯罪，死后经三道轮回：首先做狗，然后是食肉动物和驴子，最后复生为婆罗门。
学生对师父的妻子动淫念，成为有罪的人，将经受若干轮回：首先生而为狗三年，然后再生为蠕虫一年，最后复生为婆罗门。
师父无缘无故杀死像儿子一般的学生，死后生为天鹅。
人子瞧不起父亲或母亲，死后变成驴子生活十个月，然后再生为狗十四个月，再以猫为身七个月，最后复获人身。
A person who shouts at their mother and father will be reborn as a thrush in the next life.
If they actually strike their parents, they will be reborn as a turtle.
After ten years as a turtle, they become a porcupine for three years, then a snake for six months, before returning to human form.
Someone who eats their master's food while harming them becomes a monkey after death.
After ten years as a monkey, they become a mouse for three years, then a dog for six months, before returning to human form.
Someone who misappropriates entrusted property goes to Yama's realm and undergoes 100 rebirths, ending as a worm.
After fifteen years as a worm, they gradually reduce their demerits and return to human form.
A malicious person becomes a shalanka bird after death.
A deceitful, treacherous person becomes a fish after death.
After eight years as a fish, they become a deer for four months, then a ram for one year, then an insect, before returning to human form.
A thief of grains and crops becomes a mouse after death.
After death as a mouse, they become a boar, then die immediately from disease, then become a dog for five years before returning to human form.
Someone who touches another's wife becomes a wolf, then successively a dog, jackal, vulture, snake, heron, and crane.
Someone who desires his brother's wife becomes a male cuckoo for one year.

An adulterer with friend's wife, teacher's wife, or king's consort becomes a boar for five years, then a porcupine for five years, then an ant for six months, then other insects for one month, then a worm for thirteen months before returning to human form.
Someone who obstructs weddings, charity distributions, or sacrifices becomes a worm in the next life.
A person who breaks dharma will live as a worm for fifteen years.
A person who promises his daughter in marriage then gives her to another will become a worm after death.
A person who eats offerings meant for gods or ancestors before rituals will become a crow in next life.
After being a crow for ten years, the person becomes a rooster for one month, then returns to human form.
A person who disrespects their elder brother will become a snipe after death.
A Shudra who has relations with a Brahmin woman will become a worm in next life.
If the Shudra fathers a child with the Brahmin woman, he becomes a rat in next life.
Evil persons go to Yama's realm and suffer various tortures before reincarnation.
After punishments, the person reincarnates as worm for fifteen years, then dies repeatedly in womb before becoming animal.
After animal death, the person suffers more years, then becomes turtle in final birth before human rebirth.

attributes.outcome: Returns to human form after dharma restored

extraction_text: A person who kills an unarmed person for property or malice becomes donkey after death.
After donkey is killed by weapon, it becomes deer living in constant fear for one year.
After deer is killed by weapon, it becomes fish living four months before being caught in net.
After fish death, becomes carnivorous animal for ten years, then leopard for five years.

attributes.outcome: Returns to human form after dharma restored

extraction_text: A foolish person who kills a woman suffers in Yama's realm, reincarnates twenty times, then becomes worm for twenty years.
A person who steals food becomes bee in next life.
A person who steals someone else's musical instrument will be reborn as a mosquito after death.
A person who steals sesame oil cakes will be reborn as a red-haired rat after death.
A person who steals salt will be reborn as a cricket in the next life.
A person who steals yogurt will be reborn as a heron in the next life.
A person who steals and drinks milk will be reborn as a crane in the next life.
A person who steals sesame oil will be reborn as a beetle in the next life.
A person who foolishly steals honey will be reborn as a gadfly in the next life.
A person who steals iron implements will be reborn as a crow in the next life.
A person who steals milk porridge will be reborn as a partridge in the next life.
A person who steals bread will be reborn as an owl in the next life.
A person who steals fruits, roots, or cakes will be reborn as an ant in the next life.
A person who steals copper will be reborn as a Harita bird in the next life.
A person who steals silver will be reborn as a pigeon in the next life.
A person who steals gold will be reborn as a worm in the next life.
A person who steals cotton cloth will be reborn as a snipe; after dying as a snipe, they will be reborn as a human.
A person who steals cloth, wool, or takes someone's linen garment without permission will be reborn as a rabbit after death.
A person who steals multi-colored items will be reborn as a peacock after death.
A person who steals red cloth will be reborn as a partridge after death.
A person who steals ointments or perfumes will be reborn as a mole in the next life.
A person who misappropriates property entrusted to them will be reborn as a fish after death.
After being reborn as a fish and dying, the person will be reborn as a human again, but will have a short life.

attributes.action: Rebirth as human with short life

extraction_text: People who commit various sins will be reborn as animals in the next life.
People who commit faults but try to atone through penance will experience mixed fortune and disease in the future.
People prone to sin, confused, and greedy will be reborn as despised barbarians.
People who avoid sin throughout life will have health, beauty, and prosperity.
Women who fall into faults will be reborn as wives of the previously mentioned creatures.
The speaker explains that these teachings about misappropriation were heard directly from Brahma with gods present.
The speaker concludes by advising the listener to focus their mind on dharma.
